label: Keep the current first-glance hierarchy and spacious framing: the 64 px title, 28 px subtitle, 24 px section labels, 20 px nodes, 16 px supporting text, white board section, generous margins, aligned key, and source line create a legible entry order; user-flow, ER, and gantt examples show distinct layouts while retaining the same title and key grammar. Preserve meaning-based color, shape, and key semantics across types: kind-to-shape/color mappings are shared, the pink accent is reserved for the chosen first-glance object, and the key explains marks; sequence arrows, state roles, and architecture lanes deliberately retain different type-specific semantics within that common grammar. Prioritize compact back-edge routing and sequence overview legibility: state-board.png and state-on-existing-board.png show return transitions making long perimeter loops, process-board.png shows long lane trunks, and sequence-board.png is the lowest-scoring type at 19/22 while keeping a much taller lifeline layout; the gallery scores the other seven boards 21–22/22. Tune route length, label placement, and type-specific density without weakening read-back fidelity. Unify the design score contract before changing visuals: quality-rubric.md Section 7 scores eight criteria out of 16, while the playbook and screenshot README use a 22-point total with extra crossings, shared-trunk, label-collision, hygiene, and reply checks; the current gallery therefore cannot be compared from the rubric alone. Name one canonical 22-point scorecard or explicitly label the 16-point design subtotal and its six operational points. The design record is split across a style guide, JavaScript constants, Python checks, and a hand-copied Project composer: the guide claims to be the one source for color/type/spacing, but SHAPE, TINT, KINDS, TYPE, GRID and gaps live in compose-board.js, accepted pairs live in common.py, and the Project mirror parity check compares the compact JavaScript block only. This creates a clear need for a validated shared specification while preserving the current swatch and contrast rules.
